title: OSHA Stair Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1910.25)
subtitle: Use on a site walk-through of each stairway covered by 29 CFR 1910.25.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A; mark a whole section N/A when that stair type is not present.
For each Defect, record the stair location and what failed, report it for correction, and keep the stair out of use if it is unsafe to climb.
The manufacturer's instructions, 1910.28 rail rules and site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: General stairway conditions
items: Handrails, stair rails and guardrails installed as 1910.28 requires; none missing or removed
At least 6 ft 8 in (203 cm) from each tread's front edge to the nearest overhead obstruction (spiral stairs: see section D)
Every riser in the flight the same height and every tread the same depth, including the first and last step before a landing
Each landing and platform is no narrower than the stair
Landings and platforms measure 30 in (76 cm) or more in the direction of travel
A platform exists wherever a door or gate opens directly onto the stair
Door swing, platform installed before January 17, 2017
With the door or gate fully open, 20 in (51 cm) or more of usable platform depth remains
Door swing, platform installed on or after January 17, 2017
With the door or gate fully open, 22 in (56 cm) or more of usable platform depth remains
Each stair can support at least five times the normal anticipated live load, and no less than 1,000 lb (454 kg) concentrated at any point

sections.title: Choice of stair type
items: Standard stairs serve every route between levels used regularly and routinely, including to equipment operating platforms
Any winding stairway is on a tank or similar round structure with a diameter of 5 ft (1.5 m) or more
Where spiral, ship or alternating tread stairs are used, the employer can show why standard stairs are not feasible at this location
Installation, use and maintenance of these non-standard stairs match the manufacturer's instructions

sections.title: Standard stairs
items: Pitch measures 30 to 50 degrees from horizontal
No riser taller than 9.5 in (24 cm)
No tread shallower than 9.5 in (24 cm)
22 in (56 cm) or more between vertical barriers
Where risers or treads fall outside C2 or C3: dimensions match Table D-1, or the combination gives the 30 to 50 degree angle

sections.title: Spiral stairs
items: 26 in (66 cm) or more of clear width
Every riser 9.5 in (24 cm) or less
6 ft 6 in (2 m) or more above each tread, taken at its front edge
7.5 in (19 cm) or more, measured 12 in (30 cm) out from the narrow edge

sections.title: Ship stairs and alternating tread-type stairs
items: Slope measures 50 to 70 degrees from horizontal
Vertical rise between tread surfaces is 6.5 to 12 in (17 to 30 cm)
Each tread 4 in (10 cm) deep or more
Each tread 18 in (46 cm) wide or more
Tread series slopes at 50–70 degrees from horizontal
Handrails 17 to 24 in (51 to 61 cm) apart
Each tread 8.5 in (22 cm) deep or more
Risers are open wherever tread depth is under 9.5 in (24 cm)
Each tread 7 in (18 cm) wide or more at the nosing

references: 29 CFR 1910.25: Stairways (Part 1910 Subpart D, Walking-Working Surfaces)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, text as of 2026-11-09
